title: Protein Crystallization Segmentation and Classification Using Subordinate Color Channel in Fluorescence Microscopy Images
abstract: The accuracy of detecting protein crystals for fluorescence microscopy images is very critical for high throughput and automated systems. Although the trace fluorescent labeling method could highlight protein crystals, reflection and emission from the fluorescence dye is not always due to crystal regions. Therefore, the analysis of the peak wavelength in the emission spectra of a fluorophore may not always yield effective results. In this paper, we show that using the subordinate color intensity corresponding to longer wavelengths than the peak wavelength of the emission spectra could improve the accuracy of protein crystal detection. Hence, we have built a segmentation method based on the percentile intensity of the subordinate color for trace fluorescently labeled (TFL'd) protein crystallization trial images. Compared to using the dominant color channel, our segmentation method on subordinate color channel was able to reduce the misclassification rate of likely-leads or crystals as non-crystals by the percentage of from 9.71% to 2.02% depending on the classifier. Similarly, the accuracy of classifiers were increased by the percentage of from 1.77% to 5.53%. Our method reached around 94% accuracy while keeping misclassification of likely-leads and crystals as non-crystals below 1%. Moreover, to evaluate the generalizability of our method, we have conducted new wet lab experiments on two proteins, Concanavalin A (Con A) and Ab inorganic pyrophosphate (AbIPPase), and the misclassification rate was below 1%. Our experiments show that using the subordinate channel may be more helpful for TFL'd protein trial image classification.

title: An Atomic-Scale Chemical Switch for Oxide Ferroelectricity
abstract: Interfacial chemistry offers new opportunities for designing ferroelectric materials, yet their coupling with intrinsic polarization remains largely unexplored. Here, we synthesize ferroelectric BiFeO3 nanoparticles with {100} facets covered by a Bi2FeO6-x Aurivillius-like phase, allowing the interfacial Bi2O2 layer to interact with bulk polarization at different relative orientations.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Wavelength-Selective Magneto-Optical Diodes Based on Rare-Earth Chiral Molecular Crystals
abstract: Chiral materials, integrating structural breaking of mirror-symmetry, exhibit physical properties that cannot be observed in centrosymmetric analogues. Among these properties, optical magneto-chiral anisotropy, the nonreciprocal absorption of light shown by chiral magnetized systems, is emerging as an enabling technology in magneto-optics and photonics. Here, we report on enantiopure chiral molecular crystals based on the erbium(III) rare-earth ion that display nonreciprocal, wavelength-selective, magnetic field-induced variations of the optical absorption coefficients up to ca.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: PeTFlow: Flow-Matching Based All-Atom Peptide Design through Side-Chain State Tokenization
abstract: Peptide offers a powerful modality for targeting protein-protein interfaces, yet their computational design remains challenging because sequence identity, backbone geometry and side-chain packing must be optimized simultaneously within a three-dimensional pocket constrained environment. Here we present PeTFlow, a pocket-conditioned all-atom peptide co-design framework that rationalizes this constrained design problem through discrete side-chain state tokenization. In PeTFlow, each residue is represented as a chemically compatible state token, enabling unified modeling of peptide sequence, conformation and all-atom interface geometry. PeTFlow achieved superior generation quality on peptide-design benchmarks and can further be applied to therapeutically relevant peptide drug design.

title: TRF2 mediates force-resistant bridging of distal telomeric DNA repeats
abstract: Shelterin binds telomeres, regulates telomere length, and protects chromosome ends from mis-repair, which is essential for genome stability. Telomere end-protection uniquely depends on the TRF2 subunit, which assembles telomeric DNA into a protective T-loop structure in vivo, yet the biochemical mechanism underlying this process remains unresolved. Using single-molecule optical tweezers and atomic force microscopy, we show that the human shelterin complex tethers distal telomeric DNA repeats, looping the intervening DNA. These bridges withstand tens of piconewtons of applied load, rupture at a force that scales with telomeric repeat number and re-form on relaxation. Structure-function analysis demonstrates that this force-resistant tethering is TRF2-dependent under our conditions and depends on multiple interfaces, with the TRFH domain making a major but non-exclusive contribution: introducing the TRF2 TRFH domain into TRF1 is sufficient to confer tethering, whereas its deletion from TRF2 reduces but does not abolish activity. We propose telomeric dsDNA tethering by TRF2 as a candidate first step in T-loop formation, preceding invasion of the telomeric 3' ssDNA overhang.

title: JustEvo: A Prior-Guided Adaptive Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Multifunctional Protein Directed Evolution
abstract: Machine-learning-guided directed evolution can reduce the experimental burden of protein engineering by prioritizing variants before they are tested. In practice, however, many campaigns begin with few or no target-specific measurements, face choices about how to use heterogeneous protein-model priors, and require functional improvement to be balanced with developability properties such as expression and stability. Here, we present JustEvo, a closed-loop framework for low-data and multifunctional protein evolution.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Automatic insect identification, counting, and monitoring techniques: a review
abstract: BackgroundInsect pests threaten agricultural productivity, while conventional surveillance is labour-intensive and excessive pesticide use creates environmental and health risks. This review evaluated automated insect detection, counting, classification and monitoring technologies, focusing on machine-learning integration, field transferability, and operational readiness.ResultsA PRISMA 2020-guided formal search covering publications from 2010 to 2024 identified 313 records relevant to the technological and methodological scope of the review.

title: A Scalable One-Pot Strategy for Porphyrin Metal–Organic Frameworks via In situ Linker Synthesis
abstract: Porphyrin metal–organic frameworks (pMOFs) are highly versatile materials for catalysis, energy, and environmental applications, yet their widespread use is limited by the cost and multistep synthesis of porphyrin linkers. Here, we report a one-pot synthetic strategy that integrates porphyrin formation and MOF crystallization, enabling the direct assembly of zirconium-based pMOFs from simple molecular precursors. This approach eliminates the need for linker isolation and purification, significantly reducing synthetic complexity and resource consumption.

title: Hierarchical generative modeling for the design of multi-component systems
abstract: The functionality of catalysts, enzymes, and supramolecular assemblies emerges not from individual molecules alone, but from the subtle interplay between multiple components arranged in complex systems. Designing such systems is a grand challenge: the combinatorial explosion of possible chemical compositions and spatial arrangements makes brute-force exploration infeasible, while many current generative approaches remain limited to isolated molecules. In this work, we introduce a hierarchical generative optimization framework that overcomes this barrier by coupling a genetic algorithm for configurational search with a generative model for molecular design. This closed-loop approach enables simultaneous refinement of geometry and composition, efficiently steering discovery toward systems with targeted functionality. As a proof of concept, we design catalytic environments for the Claisen rearrangement of p-tolyl ether by optimizing surrounding components around a fixed reference transition-state geometry. Despite this constraint during the search phase, post-hoc validation via Climbing-Image Nudged Elastic Band calculations, with the environment held fixed, indicates a reduction of the activation barrier by about 30%. Beyond this example, the framework applies to systems in which a well-defined central structure is stabilized by non-covalently interacting components, such as supramolecular hosts and local catalytic environments.

title: Precision medicine in MASLD: Integrating genetics, multi-omics, and artificial intelligence for risk stratification and targeted therapy
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly termed nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), encompasses a heterogeneous clinical spectrum ranging from isolated hepatic steatosis to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Differences in susceptibility to disease, progression and extrahepatic complications between individuals are due to many different variables, such as genetic, metabolic and environmental factors, sex, reproductive status and gut microbiota.
venue: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry

title: Reversion to the Meta Body Form of Life after Complete Cell Death in Pure Liquid Water
abstract: The prevailing view holds that simpler animate beings predating the dawn of cellular life once existed, yet they have long since vanished from the present-day Earth. Our hypothesis posits that these animate beings persist to this day. To this end, we devised a long-term experiment spanning over a decade, keeping Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) within a sealed aqueous system of pure water. The findings illustrated that, upon the complete cell death (CCD) of the S. aureus, as cellular remnants progressively succumbed to dissolution, the aqueous solution underwent self-purification, bringing forth a class of lipid bilayer membrane microspheres containing RNA and proteins. These structures maintained long-term sustainable stability within the thermodynamic storm of water molecules and underwent dynamic size fluctuations over time - collectively exhibited phenomena indicative of being "alive". This study reveals that the cell, upon complete cell death, undergoes reversion to a living entity simpler than the cell itself - the Meta Body (MB). The discovery of MB opens an entire re-conceptualization of what death ultimately brings.

title: Understanding when and how knowledge graphs add value to EHR-based clinical prediction across Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis, and chronic pain
abstract: Biomedical knowledge graphs (KGs) have emerged as a promising approach for incorporating biological knowledge into machine-learning models trained on electronic health record (EHR) data. However, their large scale and heterogeneous structure impose substantial computational cost, and it remains unclear whether their benefits generalize across diseases or depend on how the graph is constructed. We systematically evaluated KG integration across three diseases spanning distinct biological and clinical characteristics: multiple sclerosis, Parkinson’s disease, and chronic pain.

title: Microglia transcriptomic response to doxorubicin-induced genotoxic stress
abstract: Chemobrain, characterized by cognitive dysfunction, has emerged as a significant health concern following cancer treatment. Doxorubicin, an FDA-approved chemotherapeutic agent, is widely used to treat various cancers. However, its adverse effects raise concerns regarding toxicity in non-cancerous cell types. Microglia, the resident immune cells of the brain, play a central role in maintaining neural homeostasis. Despite this, the mechanisms by which microglia become dysfunctional following doxorubicin exposure remain poorly understood. Understanding the transcriptomic alterations induced by doxorubicin in microglia could provide critical insights into mechanisms underlying its neurotoxic effects. In this study, the transcriptomic response of human microglia to doxorubicin using mRNA sequencing combined with bioinformatic analysis was investigated. Exposure to doxorubicin significantly altered microglial morphology, promoting a shift toward a process-bearing phenotype in human HMC3 cells. This phenotypic change was accompanied by elevated levels of DNA damage and was associated with the induction of cellular senescence. At the gene regulation level, the Illumina-based transcriptomic analysis provided 25,834 gene expression profiling in which 5,669 were differentially expressed. The future analyses revealed that 3,431 (upregulated) and 2,238 (downregulated) were differentially expressed under the treatment of doxorubicin. Genes associated with the p53 signaling pathway and inflammatory responses were upregulated, whereas genes involved in translation, DNA replication, and cell-cycle progression were downregulated. This transcriptional dysregulation was accompanied by differential expression of key transcription factors. This study provides transcriptomic evidence elucidating the genotoxic response to doxorubicin in microglial cells, offering mechanistic insights into chemobrain and highlighting key molecular pathways as potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

title: Human Intestinal Absorption Revisited: The 1998 Descriptors Survive, and the Method Extends to Permeability
abstract: In 1998 we predicted percent human intestinal absorption for 86 drug and drug-like compounds from six molecular descriptors chosen by a genetic algorithm and a small neural network. That result rested on one division of the compounds into training, cross-validation and external prediction groups. Repeating the division shows it was a fortunate one. Across 250 stratified extractions, 14 match the published cross-validation error and only one matches the published external prediction error.

title: Data-Driven Prediction of Speech-in-Noise Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Machine Learning Models
abstract: PurposeDifficulty understanding speech in noise (SIN) is a major determinant of communication ability and quality of life, affecting individuals with hearing loss as well as some with normal hearing. Data-driven prediction methods offer a promising approach for modeling complex, multidimensional factors underlying speech perception. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated computational approaches for predicting SIN-related outcomes, compared predictive performance across model classes where quantitative synthesis was feasible, and identified methodological factors relevant to model…

title: DSCrisk: A dual-view and substructure aware based method for drug-drug interaction risk-level prediction enhanced by contrastive learning
abstract: Combination pharmacotherapy remains a fundamental strategy in contemporary clinical practice. However, the concurrent use of multiple drugs substantially increases the risk of harmful drug-drug interaction events (DDIEs). Developing reliable computational methods for DDIE detection is therefore essential, yet existing approaches still face notable limitations in modelling interaction-relevant chemistry, relational context, and interpretability.

title: Construction and Validation of a Diagnostic Model for Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Based on Pyroptosis-Related Genes
abstract: Background: GERD is a common chronic digestive disorder, yet its diagnosis remains challenging due to the lack of objective molecular markers are lacking. Pyroptosis may contribute to esophageal mucosal injury, but a systematic search for pyroptosis-related diagnostic genes in GERD has not been performed. In this study, we used integrated bioinformatics, machine learning, and experimental validation to identify pyroptosis-associated diagnostic biomarkers for GERD and examine their relationship with the esophageal immune microenvironment.

title: Synergy of Solid-State NMR and Dielectric Spectroscopy Reveals Synchronized Multi-Rotor Dynamics in Crystalline Supramolecular Gyroscopes
abstract: Understanding the correlated dynamics of multiple molecular rotators in crystalline supramolecular assemblies is essential for designing functional molecular machines, yet deconvoluting the motions of distinct components remains inherently challenging due to the limitations of individual techniques. Here, we report a synergistic approach that combines solid-state Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (SSNMR) and dielectric spectroscopy to quantitatively resolve multirotor dynamics in a family of isostructural supramolecular gyroscopic complex architectures composed of alkyl ammonium, crown ether, and…

title: Localized Joule heating and carbonization process optimization of 3D printed polymer structures for lab-on-CMOS applications
abstract: Use of carbon electrodes integrated with CMOS technology has great promise for lab-on-chip, biomedical, environmental, and industrial applications. One method of developing carbon electrodes is to 3D print polymer nanostructures on a CMOS chip, and use a thermal annealing process to pyrolyze them into carbon at high temperature, approximately 950 °C. Such high temperature is detrimental to the CMOS sensor circuits, causing severe degradation. We present a novel solution of localized Joule heating of these polymer nanostructures to achieve complete carbonization of the electrodes. Both analytical and COMSOL simulations guided the experiments to characterize the carbonization process conditions. Partial carbonization was achieved at 500-600 °C of global temperature, and complete carbonization was achieved by localized Joule heating. Pyrolized nanostructures monolithic samples on a silica wafer were fabricated using standard material processing, such as 2-Photon Polymerization. Pyrolysis was achieved by Rapid Thermal Processing (RTP). Observations using optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy demonstrated the feasibility of polymer carbonization within a CMOS compatible temperature window.

title: Framework for an AI-Ready ARPES Community Database
abstract: Condensed matter stands to gain profoundly from widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). However, its current means of data organization impedes this endeavor. As a premier measure of electronic structure underlying material properties, Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) has accumulated over four decades of spectra, yet the community's publication-centered workflow preserves only a highly selected fraction of its experimental record. A shared data ecosystem could transform these fragmented measurements and their contexts into a persistent, collective scientific memory, creating immediate value for reproducibility and reuse while laying the foundation for AI-enabled discovery. In this Perspective, we report outcomes of a recent community workshop and propose a practical path toward such an ecosystem. Its benefits unfold along three timescales. In the near term, standardized, searchable, and citable datasets strengthen analysis pipelines independently of AI. In the intermediate future, community-validated tools operating across laboratories could enable broader reuse and increasingly closed-loop automated experiments. In the long term, a diverse corpus of measured electronic spectra could support foundation models for quantum matter. Looking forward, a diverse corpus of measured electronic spectra could support foundation models for quantum matter and new discoveries. We discuss lessons from existing scientific databases, the current state of AI in ARPES, as well as areas of community convergence on data organization, access, credit, governance, and a staged pilot program.

title: FragFlex: Fragment-Based Flexible Molecular Generation for Exploring Vast Chemical Space
abstract: Drug discovery requires efficient exploration of an astronomically large chemical space. Molecular graph diffusion models offer a promising approach to this task, but many require graph size to be fixed before generation. Although atom-level insertion and deletion can enable flexible-size generation, jointly modeling molecular size, atom types, and bonds while maintaining chemical validity remains challenging. We introduce FragFlex, a flexible-length discrete diffusion model that performs node insertion and deletion at the fragment level. During denoising, FragFlex jointly learns the size, fragment identities, and inter-fragment connectivity of the fragment graph. A neural attachment-site predictor and valence-aware assembler then convert the generated fragment graph into an atom-level molecule. In large-scale experiments generating 10 million molecules, FragFlex achieves near-perfect chemical validity while maintaining high uniqueness, demonstrating a strong balance between the two.

title: DC-Flow: Target-Conditioned Cyclic Peptide Design via Delayed-Coupling Flow Matching
abstract: Target-conditioned cyclic peptide design requires coordinating interfacial side chains with macrocyclic closure. Existing end-to-end generators concurrently update geometric and chemical variables from noise, assigning residues to disordered coordinates. Meanwhile, predictor-assisted workflows often get stuck in local traps because they lack feedback in the propose-and-filter stage and ignore 3D structural proposals during sequence search. To overcome the drawbacks of these two paradigms, we propose DC-FLOW, a staged generative framework built around Delayed-Coupling Flow Matching. In principle, DC-FLOW postpones sequence and side-chain activation until a target-conditioned backbone takes shape, resolving structural ambiguity before chemical assignment. Then, it feeds delayed activations back into the backbone, achieving co-evolution of backbone geometry and emerging residue identities by coupling their flows. This mechanism enables more reliable macrocyclic closure and favorable interface packing. For predictor-assisted workflows, DC-FLOW supplies 3D proposals with in-trajectory guidance, enabling cascaded test-time scaling to prune redundant backbones and terminate unpromising refinement early. Extensive experiments show that DC-FLOW improves cyclization fidelity, diversity, and interface energetics, substantially increasing the yield of confident cyclic peptide binders under a fixed final-candidate budget. Our code is available at https://github.com/mianqiu00/DCFlow.

title: Three-dimensional reconstruction of weakly scattering objects from single-defocus 4D-STEM data
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) atomic-structure analysis is of central importance in (scanning) transmission electron microscopy (STEM). STEM techniques to reconstruct 3D structure include tilt-series or defocus-series annular dark-field, best suited to heavier atomic species, and dynamical-scattering-model inversion applied to single-defocus four-dimensional (4D) STEM data, requiring computationally expensive post-experiment analysis. In this study, we propose a 3D-structure linear inversion (3D LINV) STEM algorithm, which enables a fast and direct reconstruction of 3D structures from a single-defocus 4D-STEM dataset. This method is based on solving linear equations relating the measured 4D-STEM data and the unknown 3D specimen potential under the thick weak phase object approximation. We show the capabilities of 3D LINV STEM through systematic 4D-STEM simulations across various observation parameters such as specimen thickness, partial coherence, and shot noise, and through an experimental demonstration of 3D structure reconstruction of a stacked freestanding membrane with atomic-scale lateral resolution and nanometre-scale depth resolution.

title: Programmable memristive circuits for reconfigurable collective pseudomagnetic ordering, transport, and learning
abstract: Programmable hardware typically uses fixed architectures, whereas complex physical systems obtain diverse behavior by connecting reusable local elements through different interaction rules. Memristive devices combine writable states with nonlinear dynamics, but translating these local properties into reconfigurable collective order and symmetry-governed transport remains challenging. Here we develop modular circuits configured through programmable connections between identical memristive units. Experiments establish binary conductance states as Ising-type pseudospins and show that signed feedback between units selects uniform or staggered pseudospin order. Circuit-model simulations then examine controllable domain-wall motion and pattern recovery. A symmetry encoder combines measured conductance patterns with sublattice labels and a selected symmetry rule to configure a fixed transport layer, implementing circuit analogs of ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and altermagnetic transport symmetries. Although the antiferromagnetic and altermagnetic encodings share a compensated pattern, their distinct voltage spreading illustrates how programmed circuit symmetry affects transport. Device-calibrated simulations show that memristive dynamics generates history-dependent features for reservoir computing. By separating local memory from programmable interactions, symmetry encoding and task-specific readout, this architecture provides a modular route from device dynamics to collective order, symmetry-dependent transport, and learning.

title: Microscopic foundation for orbitronics: orbital exchange interactions, orbital-dependent transport, and orbital switching
abstract: Recent experiments highlighted the essential role of the orbital degrees of freedom underlying current-induced magnetic dynamics. However, a microscopic picture of how orbital angular momenta are transferred between itinerant and localized electrons, and the way it feeds back into transport, remains elusive. Here we develop a theoretical framework for the orbital exchange interactions by generalizing the Anderson-Kondo model to incorporate the orbitals of conduction bands. Illustrating with the $p$-orbitals, we determine the way electrons acquire orbital polarization and its influence on the transport properties, uncovering the orbital counterparts of phenomena analogous to spin filtering and tunnel magnetoresistance. Reciprocally, we demonstrate that orbital-polarized currents can exert torques on localized magnetic moments without having to convert into spin currents, which enables electrical switching of magnetization even when spin polarization becomes inactive. These striking discoveries lay a microscopic foundation for orbitronics and reveal critical mechanisms for orbital manipulations of magnetic order.

title: Tersoff-NN: Hybrid Machine-Learned Bond-Order Extension of the Tersoff Potential
abstract: Accurate, robust, and efficient interatomic potentials are highly desirable for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Although machine-learning interatomic potentials can reproduce first-principles potential-energy surfaces with high accuracy, they typically incur higher computational costs than conventional empirical potentials and may be less reliable outside their training domains. We developed Tersoff-NN, a hybrid machine-learning potential for Si, which retains the analytical radial interactions and cutoff structure of the Tersoff potential while representing its environment-dependent bond-order factor using compact neural networks (NNs). Benchmarks for 32,768-atom systems show that Tersoff-NN is 4-12 times faster than the Behler-Parrinello-type NN potentials tested in this study. Tersoff-NN improves the short-range structure of liquid Si relative to the conventional Tersoff potential, closely reproduces the ab initio radial and angular distributions, and reproduces the equilibrium structure of diamond Si and qualitative energetic trends among several crystalline phases. Furthermore, melt-quench simulations reveal a disordered solid with predominantly four-coordinated, tetrahedral-like local environments. Additionally, characteristic reconstruction motifs are retained on Si surfaces despite their exclusion from the training dataset. A direct comparison with an alternative atom-centered bond-order NN highlights the critical role of physical constraints in ensuring dynamic stability. Despite exhibiting comparable validation errors, the selected triplet-based architecture remains stable, while an alternative model exhibits unphysical bond-order growth and atomic collapse. These results confirm that learning only the bond-order term improves the description of diverse Si environments while retaining substantial computational efficiency and enhancing dynamical stability.

title: Unlocking the potential of polymer networks for high strength through topology
abstract: A covalent polymer network is orders of magnitude weaker than individual covalent bonds. This large gap reveals an unrealized potential. The weakness of a network comes not from individual covalent bonds, but from how they are connected. Here we unlock this potential by identifying a topological criterion, involving optimally sparse crosslinks, long chains, and dense entanglements. Optimizing each topological variable alone is insufficient for high strength, yet exceptional strength emerges when they are combined within a narrow regime. We describe the physics of this synergy, and use the criterion to strengthen networks widely used but known to be weak. For example, we prepare a polyacrylamide hydrogel of 90 wt% water, amplifying strength from a commonly reported value of ~0.1 MPa to ~6.5 MPa. The exceptional strength is achieved without sacrificing other properties, such as softness, toughness, and elasticity. The criterion establishes topology as a general design principle for strong polymer networks.

title: Generalized Constraint-Controlled Rheological Model: Two Constitutive Pathways under Sinusoidal Periodic Shear Deformation
abstract: We formulate the Generalized Constraint-Controlled Rheological Model (GCCRM) for entangled linear and long-arm-branched polymer melts under sinusoidal periodic shear deformation (SPSD), spanning the linear and strongly nonlinear regimes. Molecular architecture, conformation, chain stretch, flow-active constraints, convective constraint release, dynamic tube dilation, and activated arm retraction define a common upstream molecular state. This state feeds two time-domain constitutive pathways (a configurational stress and a dissipative internal-variable stress) which are recombined before Fourier analysis. For branched polymers, the architecture is described by an entire backbone of molecular weight $M_{bb}$ and $N_a$ long arms of molecular weight $M_a$, with a compliance-weighted representative-constitutive-cell partition. The linear limit is normalized so that the configurational moduli sum to the entanglement modulus, while dynamic tube dilation and stretch drive distinct contributions to dissipative activation. Under reduced closures, GCCRM generates a smooth nonlinear elastic response with an onset of nonlinearity, an approximately logarithmic growth regime, an architecture-dependent maximum, and distinct high-deformation asymptotes. Fourier harmonics, ELR, VLR, and Lissajous curves are treated as post-processing observables of the total stress. The framework establishes a consistent constitutive architecture whose quantitative validation requires one parameter set per material across SPSD and, prospectively, transient shear histories.

title: Enhancement of local magnetic ordering temperature due to non-magnetic disorder in anti-Heusler alloy Al$_2$MnCu
abstract: Structural disorder is generally regarded as detrimental to magnetism. Since magnetic properties are governed by both the arrangement of magnetic atoms and the crystal environment, including non-magnetic atoms that mediate exchange interactions, the distinct role of magnetic and non-magnetic disorder remains less understood. The recently reported anti-Heusler alloy, Al$_2$MnCu, forming with $\sim$50\% intra-symmetry site disorder (B2) involving the magnetic Mn atom and $\sim$5\% inter-symmetry site disorder associated with non-magnetic Al and Cu atoms, offers a good platform to disentangle the individual roles of magnetic and non-magnetic atomic disorder. Our magnetic critical analysis, in the vicinity of the Curie temperature ($T_{\rm C}$), does not lead to any conventional single universality class expected for a standard ferromagnet; instead, the non-monotonic temperature dependence of effective critical exponents points towards more complex magnetic interactions, akin to inhomogeneous ferromagnets. Dc magnetometry complemented by higher-harmonic ac magnetic susceptibility data, further confirms the persistence of locally ordered magnetic clusters above $T_{\rm C}$. Theoretical analysis establishes that the enhancement of the local magnetic ordering temperature arises directly from the strengthening of exchange interactions due to the small degree of non-magnetic disorder, whereas $T_{\rm C}$ is hardly influenced by the much larger level of magnetic-atom disorder. The combined experimental and theoretical investigations on the anti-Heusler alloy Al$_2$MnCu reveal and explain the unusual observation of nonmagnetic disorder-induced elevation of $T_{\rm C}$, providing a paradigm for the counterintuitive role of disorder in magnetic materials.

title: Hidden Spin-Valley Hall Effect and Gate-Switchable Electric Hall Effect in 2D Altermagnets
abstract: Hidden beneath the vanishing charge Hall response of altermagnets are spin-up and spin-down Hall currents of opposite sign---concealed, not absent---whose cancellation is enforced by symmetry. When these spin states are locked to distinct valleys, the hidden currents constitute a spin-valley Hall effect. Here we show that in 2D altermagnets with spin-valley-layer coupling (SVLC), a gate field unveils this hidden spin-valley Hall response.~By lifting the symmetry-enforced compensation between valleys with opposite layer polarizations, the field converts the hidden response into a net charge Hall signal, yielding a gate-switchable electric Hall effect (EHE) enabled by SVLC. Using collinear spin layer group (cSLG) theory, we classify all 158 altermagnetic cSLGs, identify 32 that support SVLC, and predict monolayer Mg$_2$Os$_2$(SO$_5$)$_2$ and the Ca(CoN)$_2$-family as candidate materials. First-principles calculations for Mg$_2$Os$_2$(SO$_5$)$_2$ reveal reversible valley splitting, a gate-switchable Hall response, and a Kerr rotation exceeding 1 mrad whose sign reverses together with the EHE signal. These results establish a symmetry-based route to all-electrical valley-spin control and identify altermagnets as promising platforms for high-performance valley transport and electrically switchable magneto-optics.

title: CondMSP: Condition-Informed and Resource-Aware Inorganic Materials Synthesis Planning
abstract: Materials synthesis planning (MSP) connects AI-driven materials discovery to experimental realization by proposing precursors, synthesis operations, and processing conditions for a target material. Existing approaches predict these components separately or in pairs and treat conditions only as a prediction target. Consequently, MSP remains centered on recipe prediction: it leaves unexplored how conditions can serve as process context for constructing synthesis routes, and it does not address which candidate routes should be executed under limited experimental resources. We propose CondMSP, which extends MSP from recipe prediction to execution-aware planning. CondMSP predicts temperature, time, and atmosphere by combining a joint predictor with variable-specific experts, and then uses these predictions both as process context, grounding the generation and retrieval of operation sequences, and as execution requirements, specifying which thermal stages can share a furnace run and at what cost. This specification is held fixed across all compared methods; within it, CondMSP ranks routes across precursor sets by a common utility and, under furnace budgets, jointly selects routes and allocates their thermal stages by constrained optimization. CondMSP improves condition and operation prediction and, under this shared constraint, raises reference-recipe recovery from 27.9% to 32.9% at three simulated furnace runs per target and from 34.7% to 40.0% at 30 trials, while a new evaluation set of 2,344 targets supports generalization beyond oxide-dominated training chemistry.

title: Knowledge Interaction in Hypernetwork-based Continual Learning: Conflict and Composition
abstract: Continual learning aims to adapt pretrained large language models (LLMs) to evolving data while preserving their pretrained capabilities. A central challenge is catastrophic forgetting: adaptation to new data can impair performance on previously learned knowledge. Since continual learning commonly changes model parameters, the model's predictions may draw on knowledge from the base model, the parameter update, and the input context. Understanding how these sources interact is essential: conflicts reveal whether new knowledge can override outdated knowledge, while multi-hop reasoning tests whether new knowledge can be composed with existing knowledge to support generalization. We study these interactions in a hypernetwork-based adaptation framework, where a shared network generates adapters from context, allowing a frozen base model to adapt without task-specific updates. We find that, under knowledge conflict, models preferentially follow the context, and their choices depend more on where knowledge is presented than on its content. We also show that context and adapter knowledge perturb the base model's representations along directions orthogonal to its clean hidden states, enabling us to derive steering vectors that control which source the model follows. In multi-hop reasoning, we find that models fail to reliably compose knowledge across the three sources, with the key breakdown arising from the interaction of the hypernetwork with both the base model and the context. Code and reproduction materials: https://github.com/missswiftie/Knowledge-Interaction-in-CL

title: Indirect prediction and screening of frustrated magnetic materials using machine learning
abstract: Magnetic frustration is commonly quantified by the frustration index, calculated from the Curie-Weiss and Neel temperatures. Because both quantities are not simultaneously available for most materials, direct prediction of the magnetic frustration index remains challenging. Here, we propose a machine learning workflow for indirect prediction of the frustration index and consequent screening of potential frustrated magnetic compounds through independent prediction of Curie-Weiss and Neel temperatures. In our work, composition-based models implemented via the CatBoost algorithm, trained on experimental data were optimized using chemically informed dataset subdivision. The highest predictive accuracy was achieved for the rare earth-oxide model in predicting Neel and for the rare earth model in predicting Curie-Weiss. Ensemble uncertainty was incorporated through a conservative frustration index to improve the reliability of candidate selection. Screening of approximately 67000 Materials Project compounds identified 20 high-confidence frustrated magnetic candidates, including several experimentally known frustrated magnets and previously unexplored oxide systems potential for further investigation.

title: Realistic Simulation of Valence-band Photoemission Spectra by using First-principles Calculations on the Basis of FLAPW Method
abstract: In order to reproduce experimental photoemission spectroscopy (PES) data by using band structure calculations with linearized augmented-plane-wave method, we developed a new method to calculate the atomic-subshell photoelectron differential cross section (PE-DCS) of the valence band. PE-DCS was calculated to be the sum of the products of the partial density of states (PDOS) and the photoionization differential cross section (PI-DCS) of each atomic subshell. To construct an appropriate PDOS beyond the conventional muffin-tin sphere (MTS) PDOS, we proposed a ``nearly-neutral atomic sphere", which can be defined as a natural extension of MTS. Although the calculational method for atomic-subshell PI-DCS was the standard Hartree-Fock-Slater method, we developed a new computer code in order to deal with the unoccupied electron shells in the ground state of isolated atoms up to $\sim$10 keV. Details of the PE-DCS calculations were examined by using two simple examples of Na metal and NaCl, and then, the method was applied to hard x-ray PES (HX-PES) data of CuAlO$_2$. The experimental spectra were satisfactorily reproduced, demonstrating the potential applications of our method to HX-PES spectra of many compounds.

title: Molecular Vibronic Complexity as a Quantum Resource for Optimal Control: Nonadiabatic Mixing Creates Protected Coherence Subspaces in Dissipative Environments
abstract: In molecules, electronic coherence typically decays within a few hundred femtoseconds, a timescale usually attributed to the environment. We show that it is set to a large extent by which coherences are excited: the molecule can host coherences that the bath barely sees, and optimal control can find and exploit them. Using gradient-based optimal control (GRAPE) with Redfield dynamics, we maximize the total vibronic coherence between the electronic ground and an optically bright electronic excited state in a three-state model with nonadiabatic features, in two regimes of low and high nonadiabatic mixing and for different system-bath coupling strengths. The Liouvillian spectrum reveals, in both regimes, a well-separated coherence mode with substantial ground-bright character that decays on a picosecond timescale. This mode is protected by mixing with the dark state, which brings the geometry of the optically accessible excited state close to that of the ground state and thus weakens its coupling to the bath. Without prior information, GRAPE finds this mode and keeps the photoexcited wave packet near the Franck-Condon region. At equal fluence, it increases the coherence at 800 fs by more than two orders of magnitude over a Gaussian pulse at the weakest coupling, and by many more at stronger coupling. The Liouvillian predicts the bath dependence of the long-lived coherence to within 1\%, and a Gaussian pulse tuned to the mode frequency comes within 10\% of the best pulse found. Beyond two-level and spin systems, our study puts forward the vibronic structure of molecules as a route to protected coherence subspaces, identifying a dark-state protection mechanism and a design criterion based on molecular parameters. These results lay the groundwork for our goal of using vibronic molecular systems as a resource for long-lived, controllable coherences in molecular quantum information science.

title: Kernel-Level Constant-Potential Molecular Dynamics in GROMACS
abstract: How charge rearranges within an electrode shapes the behavior of batteries, supercapacitors, and other electrochemical devices. Molecular simulations can capture this response by allowing the charge on each electrode atom to adjust to its surroundings, but repeatedly calculating these charges adds substantial computational cost. We present an open-source implementation of the constant-potential method in GROMACS that integrates these calculations into the program's optimized CPU and GPU routines. Comparisons with established codes validate the electrode charges, while charging, voltammetry, and impedance simulations demonstrate the response to changing electrical conditions. The implementation also supports electrodes that move or deform and models of finite metallic screening and electron spillover. In a pair of charged carbon nanotubes, allowing charge to move away from the facing surfaces reduces the repulsive force at contact by about half at an intermediate charge and keeps the pair bound where a uniform-charge model opens within the simulated time. These capabilities make the electrical response of electrodes accessible within GROMACS for studies of interfacial structure, charging dynamics, and electrode motion.

title: Uncovering the Generative Landscape of Diffusion Models: A Spectral-Guided Quality-Diversity Diffusion Framework
abstract: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models have emerged as powerful generative priors across domains ranging from molecular design to high-resolution image synthesis. However, standard diffusion sampling is inherently biased toward high-likelihood regions, often limiting the diversity of outputs. In many domains, a single, high-likelihood sample is insufficient. Instead, diverse portfolios of high-performing solutions are required, motivating methods that uncover a model's full expressive range. Here we show that integrating Quality-Diversity (QD) optimisation with diffusion models enables the discovery of diverse, high-performing outputs. We first propose Quality-Diversity Diffusion, a framework that adapts QD to diffusion models by directly optimising the model's latent noise and conditioning embeddings and leveraging embedding models to quantify diversity. Second, we introduce a novel h-space Spectral Mutation operator, which guides search along directions of maximal semantic sensitivity by analysing principal singular vectors of the model's input-to-activation Jacobian. We evaluate our combined approach, Spectral-Guided Quality-Diversity Diffusion, on text-to-image generation. Against 12 baselines, our method consistently achieves the lowest FID score, demonstrating an excellent balance of image quality and diversity.

title: Reversible intrinsic-extrinsic crossover of the anomalous Hall effect in PrAlSi via Al/Si ratio tuning
abstract: The anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in magnetic Weyl semimetals arises from distinct microscopic origins-intrinsic Berry curvature and extrinsic scattering mechanisms-yet reversible switching between these regimes within a single material platform remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that off-stoichiometric tuning of the Al/Si ratio (from ~1.05 to ~0.75) reversibly drives an intrinsic-extrinsic-intrinsic crossover of the AHE in PrAlSi single crystals. Across four compositions spanning a narrow Si variation (PrAl0.93Si0.89 to PrAl0.79Si1.06), the anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) exhibits a non monotonic arch (170-1413- 507-164 Ω-1cm-1). The intermediate composition PrAl0.90Si0.94 (Al/Si ~0.96) exhibits high carrier mobility, multi carrier transport, yielding a giant AHC of 1413 Ω-1cm-1 dominated by extrinsic skew-scattering. The Si-poor and Si-rich compositions exhibit lower AHC values and intrinsic Berry-curvature-dominated AHE, establishing a composition-driven intrinsic-extrinsic-intrinsic crossover. Deviating from the intermediate composition suppresses mobility and reverses carrier type from hole-like to electron-like. The Al/Si ratio thus serves as a chemical knob that primarily modulates the Fermi level via compositional band filling, while off-stoichiometry-induced chemical disorder plays a subordinate role in determining the AHE mechanism. These results position off-stoichiometric PrAlSi as a tunable platform where subtle compositional variation reversibly switches the AHE mechanism.

title: Ionomer-free Iridium Anodes with Low Loading for Zero-gap Electrolyzers via Direct Atomic Layer Deposition
abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is among the most promising techniques to provide hydrogen as both energy carrier and feedstock for the chemical industry, due to its compatibility with intermittent renewable electricity sources. However, a major bottleneck in scaling up PEMWE is the limited supply of the anode catalyst Ir. This work shows a novel approach to tailoring ionomer-free catalyst layers based on custom-made microporous substrates and two different atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes, both using Ir(EtCp)(CHD) precursor. Thermal ALD using O3 as counter-reactant yields mostly metallic Ir/IrOx and an electrode Ir loading of 0.21 mg/cm2. The PEMWE cell-level performance is comparable to a commercial catalyst-coated membrane anode despite 7x lower loading, and is maintained over an accelerated durability test equivalent to 600 h of intermittent operation. Moreover, using a low-loading ALD-made cathode, the total platinum group metal loading is only 0.24 mg/cm2. Plasma-enhanced ALD reduces the Ir loading to 0.04 mg/cm2 by tailoring the catalyst distribution, however, yields lower-activity IrO2. Finally, direct ALD catalyst deposition needs no ionomer-bearing ink. The anodes are therefore compatible with various membrane materials, as demonstrated in a CO2 electrolysis experiment with an anion exchange membrane.

title: A representation of the visual environment in the human basolateral amygdala supports learning and choice
abstract: Animals continuously transform sensory inputs into representations that guide behavior. Although the amygdala is a brain structure critical for learning and choice, how natural sensory experience is represented within this circuit remains unknown. Here, we identify a representation of the visual environment in the human basolateral amygdala (BLA) that contains information relevant for learning and choice. Using image-computable encoding models trained on responses to naturalistic videos, we recover a continuous, low-dimensional representation of visual experience in the BLA.

title: The RAS-CCSD model, with applications for open-shell molecules
abstract: The restricted active space coupled cluster singles and doubles (RAS-CCSD) model, and its pilot implementation is detailed. The approach offers a simple, pragmatic way to formulate a coupled cluster theory for open-shell and multireference systems. For ground state energies, errors (compared to FCI) are shown to be similar to those of unrestricted (spin-orbital) CCSD. For excited states, the errors of RAS-CCSD are generally larger, and adaptations to the methodology are needed to achieve an approach which is balanced for both ground and excited states. However, unlike unrestricted CCSD, the approach is spin-adapted and can be used to add dynamical correlation to a multideterminantal reference state.

title: Epitaxial Oxide Thin Films with High Entropy and Anomalous Crystallinity
abstract: Pulsed laser deposition (PLD) expands the compositional and structural possibilities of high-entropy oxide (HEO) thin films through far-from-equilibrium growth and kinetic arrest of metastable configurations. This review connects growth kinetics and epitaxial constraints to the roles of individual cations in shaping the resulting films. We focus primarily on rock salt MgCoNiCuZnO and its derivatives, with selected fluorite, spinel, and perovskite examples illustrating broader applicability. In MgCoNiCuZnO, Co valence and Cu coordination illustrate how chemistry and growth conditions jointly enable lattice tuning and coherent nanostructure formation, while aliovalent and size-misfit additions expand the accessible defect and compositional landscapes. These coupled degrees of freedom underpin anomalous crystallinity, the coexistence of extensive chemical disorder with exceptional crystalline quality and epitaxial order, including full coherence in selected systems, particularly rock salts grown on MgO. This combination opens opportunities to discover and engineer functional configurations in high-quality single-layer films and heterostructures.

title: Gold nanofibers as scaffolds for neuron differentiation in a 3D microtissue
abstract: Engineering neuronal tissues requires biomaterials that provide structural support while actively directing cell fate. Here, high-aspect-ratio gold nanofibers are explored as bioinstructive scaffolds for neuronal organization and differentiation. In a 2.5D paper-based model, the nanofibers guide Neuro-2a cell organization and promote neurite-like extensions through topographical interactions. Building on these findings, a printable composite bioink comprising a gelatin/alginate liquid phase and gelatin microstrands is fabricated.

title: Enhanced Spin-Forbidden Excitation of Ru(II) Polypyridyl Complexes for the Promotion of Red-Light Photocatalysis
abstract: Photoredox catalysis, mainly occurring under blue light, has emerged as an indispensable tool in modern organic synthesis. However, some limitations remain, mostly due to the high energy inherent to the irradiation wavelengths used. Red-light excitation of transition-metal photocatalysts is attractive for expanding the synthetic utility of visible-light photochemistry. Here, we report a strategy to enhance spin-forbidden red-light absorption in Ru(II) polypyridyl complexes through ligand tuning.

title: Defining Applicability Domains for Metal–Ligand Selectivity Prediction: Predictive Uncertainty vs. Molecular Similarity
abstract: Applicability domains are widely used to determine whether a machine-learning prediction can be trusted, yet they are commonly defined by similarity to the training data rather than by evidence that similarity predicts error. Here, we treat an applicability criterion as a testable claim and evaluate whether it identifies predictions with lower error than an equally sized random subset on a common held-out population.

title: Application-Specific Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis of Source-Optimized Nanoparticle Textile Formulations: Trade-offs in Washing Durability, Antibacterial Performance, and Laboratory-Scale Raw-Material Cost
abstract: Nanoparticle-functionalized textiles offer antibacterial and self-cleaning functions, but their practical suitability is difficult to compare because laundering protocols, reported performance measures, and formulation costs vary across studies. This study develops an application-specific multi-criteria decision-analysis framework using harmonized secondary data from eight source-optimized TiO2-, ZnO-, Ag-, and hybrid-based textile formulations under a school sports-bib scenario.

title: From MOF to polyMOF: Incorporation of Poly(itaconic acid) into a Cu-Ellagate Framework
abstract: The incorporation of flexible coordinating polymers into crystalline metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) remains challenging because the conformational freedom of macromolecular ligands can interfere with the development of long-range order. Here, we report IEF-35(Cu), a new Cu–ellagate MOF whose crystal structure was resolved by electron diffraction, and its extension to a polymer-containing framework, PolyIEF-35(Cu), through the incorporation of poly(itaconic acid) (PIA) as a co-ligand.

title: Unleashing AI for preclinical drug development
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping preclinical drug development across target discovery, therapeutic design, synthesis, functional characterization and safety assessment. In this review, we present an integrated view of AI across the preclinical pipeline, beginning with target identification, modality selection and representation learning for molecular, protein, structural, cellular and multimodal data.

title: From Vacuum Geometry to Solution-Phase Electronic Properties and Thermodynamics via Equivariant Neural Networks
abstract: We introduce a general framework for predicting solution-phase quantum-mechanical (QM) properties of drug-like molecules directly from gas-phase geometries, without solvent-specific structural optimization or property calculations. Using current equivariant neural network (ENN) architectures, such as MACE and Allegro, we demonstrate that they can also predict extensive and intensive QM properties in implicit water at a high level of theory.

title: The Chemical Bond in the Age of Quantum Information: Atoms in Molecules as Entangled Open Systems
abstract: The chemical bond is among the oldest ideas in chemistry and still among the least settled: chemists continue to disagree about what a bond is. We argue that the recurring controversies (ionic versus covalent, dative versus shared-electron, hypervalent versus metavalent, whether metal–metal contacts are genuinely collective) are not disputes about the physics but about an unstated reference against which a bond is declared.

title: Enabling Optoelectronics in Cu2S/Co9S8 Heteroassembly
abstract: Semiconductor heteroassembly can integrate complementary properties through nanoscale interfaces, but structural integration alone does not necessarily yield optoelectronic functionality. Here, we demonstrate an optoelectronically active Cu2S/Co9S8 heteroassembly for photodetection, obtained through higher-temperature nucleation and growth conditions that may promote enhanced crystallization and structural ordering of Co9S8. Structural characterization reveals crystalline Cu2S nanostructures decorated with dense 3–5 nm Co9S8 nanocrystallites, providing extensive interfacial contact.

title: Data-Driven Approach to Predicting Durability and Property Retention in Polymer Matrix Composites
abstract: Predicting the long-term performance of reinforced polymer composites from short-duration accelerated aging data remains a central challenge in composite durability engineering. This work presents a data-driven kinetic and mechanical-performance characterization of a glass-flake reinforced unsaturated polyester composite exposed to deionized water at 20, 40, 60 and 80 °C for up to 14.5 months, integrating long-term gravimetric sorption, flexural testing, and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA), including substantial portions of the dataset that have not previously been analyzed or reported.

title: Spirocyclic Azetidines as Lactam Bioisosteres in Isoindolinones Through Facile C1 Stitching Enabled by Dual Energy- and Electron-Transfer Photocatalysis
abstract: Bioisosteric replacement of nitrogen-containing cyclic structures with smaller, more conformationally rigid ring systems such as azetidines and spirocyclic azetidines has emerged as an effective strategy to improve the physicochemical and pharmacokinetic profiles of nitrogen-bearing drug candidates. Despite extensive studies, the use of spirocyclic azetidines as bioisosteres has been limited to simple ring systems and has not been extended to medicinally relevant complex pharmacophores.

title: Beyond Bulk Grade: Mineral–Flow Accessibility Controls Pore-Scale Copper Recovery
abstract: Mineral dissolution in porous media is driven by fluid flow, solute transport, and geochemical reactions, yet reactive transport models commonly use bulk mineral abundance and specific surface area as proxies for mineral reactivity. This neglects a key constraint: dissolution occurs only where reactants can access minerals through connected fluid-flow pathways. Here, we use pore-scale PFLOTRAN simulations of acid-driven chrysocolla dissolution to isolate the effect of mineral accessibility at fixed initial mineral volume fraction.

title: 3D DLP Printing of Multi-Responsive Cellulose Derivatives with Tunable Structural Color
abstract: Polymer systems exhibiting structural color represent a promising class of materials for 3D printing due to their capability to adapt their properties in response to external stimuli. Hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) stands out for its ability to form cholesteric liquid crystalline phases that exhibit vivid structural colors. In this work, we introduce a digital light processing strategy to fabricate complex 3D structures with tunable, stimuli-responsive structural color using methacrylated HPC (HPC-MA).

title: Transformation product bottleneck: Photo-recalcitrance of rotenolone limits the aquatic degradation of rotenone in a temperature-dependent manner
abstract: The environmental fate and toxicity of transformation products (TPs) are frequently overlooked. However, in many cases, TPs are functional analogs that exhibit similar, and often greater, toxicity as the parent compound. In cases where the TP is persistent in the environment, the rate of TP degradation can influence the overall environmental fate. Rotenolone (12𝛼-hydroxy-rotenone, ROH) is the primary TP of rotenone (ROT), a pesticide utilized ubiquitously and highly popular in cold regions.

title: FMS2Lib: A Machine Learning-Ready Tandem Mass Spectral Library for Nontargeted Analysis of Non-conventional PFAS
abstract: Nontargeted identification of non-conventional per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), including fluorinated pharmaceuticals and pesticides, remains challenging. Existing machine learning models for nontargeted analysis, primarily trained on tandem mass spectra of nonfluorinated compounds, may not generalize well to non-conventional PFAS because of their distinct mass spectrometric chemistry. Here, we established FMS2Lib, an experimental tandem mass spectral library containing 34,686 fluorinated drug-like compounds (F 1-4 ), to support machine learning-based nontargeted PFAS analysis.

title: Following Nature’s Lead – Pillar[n]arene Phosphates as Versatile Molecular Hosts
abstract: Phosphates are ubiquitous natural recognition motifs. Their charge, hydrogen bonding, variable substitution, and reversible enzymatic installation uniquely enable complex tasks in Biology. However, they are not used extensively in supramolecular systems. Herein, we combine Nature’s modulator with supramolecular rational design, creating rim-functionalised pillar[n]arene phosphates, which act as highaffinity molecular hosts. Using robust phosphoramidite chemistry, we prepared P5Max and P6Max, based on pillar[5]arene and pillar[6]arene cores in four high yielding steps.

title: Catalytic C–O Bond Cleavage of Vinyl Ethers via Dehydrovinylation and Tandem Tishchenko Coupling
abstract: The cleavage of ether C–O bonds by transition-metal complexes has attracted considerable attention, but catalytic cleavage of vinyl ether C(sp²)–O bonds is largely unexplored. Herein we report the dehydrovinylation of alkyl vinyl ethers catalyzed by a pincer-ligated osmium complex. Primary alkyl vinyl ethers undergo C–O bond cleavage to afford ethylene and the corresponding aldehydes, which undergo tandem Tishchenko coupling to yield esters. Secondary alkyl vinyl ethers undergo dehydrovinylation to afford ethylene and ketones.

title: Photochemical Aminomethylation of C(sp 3 )–H Bonds via Hydrogen Atom Transfer
abstract: Direct installation of an aminomethyl group onto aliphatic C–H bonds provides an attractive route to valuable amine-containing building blocks but remains challenging with conventional polar approaches. Here, we report a photochemical aminomethylation of C(sp3)–H bonds enabled by hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). Photoexcited benzophenone directly abstracts hydrogen from αamino, α-oxy, and α-thio C–H bonds, generating carbon-centered radicals that are intercepted by an in situ-formed N-protected formimine.

title: Rational construction of semi-clathrate-like water networks on engineered ferritin cages
abstract: Understanding and controlling the organization of water at molecular interfaces is a longstanding goal in both biological and materials sciences, as it controls the biophysical properties of the surfaces. For example, semi-clathrate waters containing polygonal hydrogen-bonded water clusters found in some antifreeze proteins (AFPs), are thought to play key roles in interacting with ice. Despite this significance, the lack of well-defined design principles makes it difficult to rationally construct such ordered hydration architectures.

title: Atomic-Scale Insights into the Surface Chemistry, Surface Stability, and Floatability of Spodumene and Montebrasite with Fatty Acid Collectors
abstract: Spodumene and montebrasite are minerals that contain significant quantities of lithium and are often found together in phosphate-rich lithium pegmatites. Separating these two minerals by flotation is key to efficient downstream lithium extraction from each. Understanding the crystal and surface properties of both minerals is an important step towards their separation by flotation. We present a systematic study of the surface properties of spodumene and montebrasite, and their interactions with fatty acid collectors, using density functional theory calculations.

title: Next Generation NPK Slow Release Hydrogel Fertilizers: A Critical Review of Material Design, Performance, and Field Translation
abstract: Climate variability, water scarcity, declining soil quality, and inefficient fertilizer use are increasing the need for nutrient-delivery systems that support climate-resilient agriculture. Slow-release fertilizer hydrogels (SRFHs) are promising because they can retain water and control nutrient transport. This critical review examines SRFHs within conventional and enhanced-efficiency fertilizer strategies. It covers matrix, coated reservoir, and multilayer systems, along with their preparation methods and functional properties.

title: Lipid-Phase Access Does Not Explain P-Glycoprotein Substrate Selection in Matched Pairs
abstract: The hydrophobic vacuum cleaner model holds that P-glycoprotein intercepts substrates within the lipid bilayer, which makes lipid-phase access to the transporter a candidate determinant of efflux, but the proposition has never been tested on compounds matched for the properties that otherwise dominate. We simulated nine matched molecular pairs—matched simultaneously on calculated lipophilicity, hydrogen-bond donors, polar surface area and molecular weight, and differing 5.9-to 30.1-fold in measured MDR1-MDCK efflux ratio—in a coarse-grained blood–brain barrier membrane containing human…

title: Direct-Write Printing of Freestanding Prussian Blue Analogue Fibers with Tunable Redox Potentials
abstract: Prussian blue (PB) and its analogues (PBAs) are attractive electrode materials for energy storage because of their chemical tunability, open-framework structures, fast ion transport, and rich redox chemistry. Yet, their practical implementation remains limited due to the challenging processability and the discrete set of redox potentials accessible through conventional compositions.

title: Beyond Materials Rankings: When Adsorption or Membranes Win for CO2/CH4 Separation
abstract: Choosing between adsorption and membranes for carbon dioxide removal from methane is often reduced to a contest between material metrics, even though an industrially meaningful answer emerges from the coupled material, flowsheet, pressure, composition, recovery, and economic context. Here we compare the technologies on a common process boundary, allowing each to select its process-optimal material, equipment size, and membrane architecture while meeting identical methane-product and recovery constraints.

title: Tunable Aza-BODIPY Photocatalysts for Near-Infrared Metallaphotoredox Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization
abstract: The merger of photoredox and transition-metal catalysis has significantly advanced radical and redox transformations, yet its reliance on UV or visible light continues to limit applications in optically complex and spatially confined environments. Herein, we introduce a modular family of tetraaryl aza-boron-dipyrromethene (aza-BODIPY) organic photocatalysts (PCs) for near-infrared (NIR) metallaphotoredox atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP).

title: A dimension staircase for orientational heat capacity: nature skips the 3/2 rung
abstract: The low-temperature orientational heat capacity of an interacting multipole pair is conventionally taken to be two-valued: 3/2 k B for axially symmetric moments and 2 k B otherwise. Here I evaluate it for all 101,666,280 molecular geometries of the OMol25 dataset and show that this is the bottom rung of a staircase: the exponent is a count, not a case split, γ = C v / k B = Σ i 1/ p i , which for two rigid nonlinear molecules is exactly γ = D / 2 and leaves only the rungs 3/2, 2 and 5/2.

title: Advancing Targeted Nanoparticle mRNA Delivery Using Machine Learning
Diverse Remote Difunctionalization of Enyne-type Propargylic Carbonates: Regio-, Chemo-, and Stereoselective Access to Highly Functionalized Multisubstituted 1,3-Dienes
abstract: Herein, we report the first catalytic heterodifunctionalization and homodifunctionalization of readily available 1-substituted enyne-type propargylic derivatives, proceeding via a multicomponent remote C2,C5-addition/substitution pathway. This palladium-catalyzed protocol enables the modular and straightforward assembly of tri-, tetra-, and penta-substituted 1,3-dienes with diverse functional groups from two heteroatom nucleophiles or one heteroatom nucleophile and one carbon nucleophile.

title: An alternative equation for effective nuclear charge that is applicable to all atoms
abstract: Although the advent of ionization energies predated Slater’s rule, there was unawareness of the utilitarian value of the former for the computation of effective nuclear charge (ENC for short) until recently and in this research. The study aimed to derive another equation in which the average ionization energies of hydrogen and any other multielectron atom are independent variables.

title: Resolving Month-Long Nanostructural Evolution in Degrading Anion Exchange Membranes
abstract: Chemical degradation reshapes the hydrated ion-transport channels of anion exchange membranes (AEMs), but conventional aging measurements do not reveal how their nanostructure evolves toward functional failure. Here we resolve this structural evolution using high-resolution kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations. The simulations are calibrated to reproduce the experimental ion exchange capacity (IEC) and water uptake (WU) over a month degradation of a PPO-TEA membrane.

title: The Dopant Cage Sets the Phonon Count of Lanthanide Emitters
abstract: Multiphonon relaxation decides whether a lanthanide ion emits light or heats its host. Since 1968 it has been predicted from the host’s maximum phonon energy, although the excitation resides on a single ion. First-principles force constants and five decades of relaxation measurements show that the accepting vibration is the stretch of the dopant’s coordination cage, a site property set by local chemistry. Aliovalent substitution stiffens the cage by up to 27%, and across seven halide hosts the cage frequency departs from the host frequency by −21% to +19%.

title: CAN it work? Using hydroxyethyl acrylate or methacrylate to turn epoxy-amine thermosets into covalent adaptable network materials.
abstract: Epoxy-amine thermosets can be converted into covalent adaptable networks (CANs) by adding β-aminoester-based curing agents to the formulation. This is achieved by utilizing commercially available di- or trifunctional acrylate monomers, which react with the amine component via an aza-Michael addition. Consequently, this approach is inherently scalable and holds high industrial relevance.

title: Lithium Plating-Induced Fracture of Individual Graphite Platelets Revealed by Operando
abstract: Lithium plating is a key barrier to achieving faster charging of lithium-ion batteries; however, fundamental and nanoscale understanding of plating is still being developed, largely due to the dynamic nature of the process. Here, we perform operando electrochemical atomic force microscopy on individual graphite platelets to observe the morphology evolution of plated lithium and graphite electrodes simultaneously. We observe plating-induced fracture of the graphite platelets even in the absence of a porous electrode structure.

title: Large language model-generated patterns for epidemiological modeling: a multi-benchmark evaluation framework
abstract: Representing individual-level behavioral heterogeneity is challenging in epidemiological modeling, particularly when empirical behavioral data are sparse. We assess the potential of large language model (LLM)-generated behavioral outputs in addressing this challenge, using hepatitis C virus-related behaviors among people who inject drugs as a case study. Correspondence with epidemiological patterns was evaluated using external benchmarks: literature-informed association directions, correlations from an agent-based model (ABM), and survey associations. Across three LLMs, unconditional directional recovery across 28 retained literature-informed associations was 46-68%, compared with 82-93% agreement when LLMs were directly asked to classify the same associations. Mean absolute differences from ABM and survey correlation patterns were 0.11-0.13 and 0.15-0.18, respectively. Together, these findings show partial alignment between LLM-generated behavioral relationships and epidemiological evidence, despite higher knowledge-probe agreement. More systematic evaluation is needed before incorporating LLM-generated behavioral outputs into epidemiological models that simulate transmission dynamics.

title: Extreme anharmonicity determines the superionic transition in the prototypical antifluorite Li$_2$O
abstract: Superionic conductors are promising electrolyte candidates for all-solid-state batteries, thanks to their liquid-like ionic mobility. In the prototypical lithium-ion oxide superionic conductor with antifluorite structure, the high-temperature transition to the fast-ion regime has long been attributed to volume-driven harmonic phonon softening. However, this quasi-harmonic picture neglects the strong lattice anharmonicity inherent to the fast-ion regime, leaving the microscopic origin of the transition unresolved. Here, we apply non-perturbative lattice dynamics combined with a first-principles-accurate machine-learning interatomic potential to study the phase transition in Li$_2$O. We demonstrate that anharmonicity, rather than volume expansion alone as commonly assumed, plays the decisive role in determining the transition temperature and the underlying mechanism. Finally, we analyze the spectral properties using the time-dependent self-consistent harmonic approximation, revealing the breakdown of the quasi-particle picture in this material. The spectral function and the infrared response provide signtures of the phase transition that can be investigated experimentally using inelastic neutron or X-ray scattering and infrared spectroscopy. All these results establish the extreme anharmonicity of Li$_2$O near the superionic regime and provide a lattice-dynamic framework for understanding and engineering the fast-ion transition in this type of materials.

title: The Anatomy of a Blind Spot: What an LLM Judge Must Be Shown, and How Much
abstract: Evaluation of text generated by large language models (LLMs) is increasingly delegated to LLMs acting as judges, yet what such a judge must be shown remains unresolved. We treat a judge whose reports are acted on as a regulator, in the sense of cybernetics, and ask what it must be shown, how much, in what form, and what its reports must get right. On seven public benchmarks we varied only what the judge was shown. Across three judges whose prices differ 10- to 17-fold, what the judge was shown mattered more than which judge it was. When a system revised its answers on feedback from a judge denied the material they had to respect, it ended below its starting point on instruction following and question answering. On instruction following the loss grew with each round, and it persisted when the judge saw the user's request but not the constraints and with a second judge family. On news summarisation, a correct reference summary beside the source undid most of the source's contribution, whereas on single-answer questions a reference helped. About a tenth of the source did almost all of its work, and a small entailment graph matched an LLM judge at finding errors in grounded text. We committed 83 testable clauses before running; of the 81 that ran, 32 met their bar and 50 went in the predicted direction, and most quantitative predictions from the theory failed. We report every shortfall and derive design rules tied to measured effects.

title: Koopman Operator Inference for the Chemical Master Equation
abstract: We infer kinetic rates of stochastic reaction networks from molecular-state pairs separated by a fixed time lag, without constructing the large state space of the Chemical Master Equation. Extended dynamic mode decomposition estimates the finite-time evolution of selected functions of the molecular state. A matrix logarithm then gives a projected generator whose species rows determine the rates through the known reaction stoichiometry. A finite set of functions introduces a systematic bias. We construct additional functions from the reaction channels and prove that each level of closure moves the first bias term to higher order. Spectral formulas identify the omitted modes responsible for this bias and show when the logarithm amplifies sampling error. Exact calculations and experiments on five reaction networks confirm the predicted error behavior and show when the added functions improve finite-sample rate recovery.

title: Transfer learning-aided, artificial intelligence approach to evaluate optical properties of materials for classical and quantum photonic applications
abstract: In this study, an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation of the refractive indices of different materials is performed. The evaluation of the refractive index is necessary to design photonic devices for various classical and quantum photonic applications, and to theoretically analyse experimental results. The refractive index is one of the crucial parameters that affect the interaction of light with matter. Although the refractive index can be measured experimentally, its estimation via computational means provide the advantage of not requiring costly instrumentation, trained researchers and could avoid potential laboratory-based uncertainties. Therefore, in this study, artificial intelligence is implemented to estimate the optical constants of two types of materials, i.e., noble metals, and semiconductors. To this end, an artificial neural network is used to estimate the real and the imaginary parts of the refractive index of a specific material for various wavelengths of light. Then, the knowledge of the trained neural network is employed to initiate and train new neural networks to estimate the refractive indices of other materials. For the training of a neural network, various methods can be deployed. However, the application of the training can be a time-consuming process. A transfer learning approach is here implemented to provide a faster training solution for the problem under study. The implementation of transfer learning allows training the neural networks for a new material with higher speed or accuracy when compared to non-knowledge transfer-based training. Our results show the efficiency of the proposed technique in accurately evaluating the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index of different materials.

title: LURE: a Phase-Labelled Synthetic Corpus of Online-Grooming Exchanges
abstract: Phase-annotated conversational data is essential for studying the progression of online grooming of minors and for developing early warning tools. However, the only publicly available source (i.e., Perverted-Justice archive, which contains a subset coded using ChatCoder) is small, outdated, and frozen.
