We present a synthetic corpus of groomer-victim exchanges, generated using a retrieval-augmented pipeline running on institutional hardware. This pipeline uses an openly available, eight-billion-parameter, refusal-ablated language model. The corpus was created using the five stages of the responsible-generation protocol for synthetic datasets: ontology-driven design based on the ChatCoder luring-communication scheme (eight communicative tags mapped onto four grooming phases); multi-model prompt testing; human-in-the-loop supervision; semantic and feature-level validation; and modality-aware documentation. The released corpus contains 2,121 unique exchanges across seven tags and four phases, each accompanied by a Plutchik emotion field. Validation quantifies the integrity and lexical profile of the corpus, as well as the reproduction of real seed lines, in-domain label recoverability (tag accuracy: 0.85; phase accuracy: 0.93) and its transfer to real ChatCoder offender lines, which were coded automatically at the eight-tag level (31,640 lines) and by human coders at the three-construct level (10,876 posts). Accuracy was measured for lexical and sentence-embedding features, while a real-versus-synthetic discriminator was able to separate the two domains with 91% accuracy. The scope of the corpus includes controlled, phase-conditioned experimentation, pipeline development and augmentation alongside real data and awareness material. The corpus, its datasheet and the audit code are released with vetted access.

title: Physics-guided machine learning for saturation control across variable hydraulic conditions in heap leaching
abstract: Heap-leaching hydraulics vary between regions of an ore bed, motivating fast prediction models that accommodate different material properties. This study develops a parameter-conditioned physics-guided machine-learning (PGML) surrogate and demonstrates its use in simulated saturation control. A dataset of 4096 numerical Richards-equation trajectories was divided into 2867 training, 614 validation and 615 evaluation cases. The network predicts hourly saturation profiles from the current profile, irrigation rate and four hydraulic parameters, and is trained with an approximate Gardner mass-balance penalty. A daily predictive controller compared 200 constant irrigation rates over a 24-hour horizon. Across the evaluation cases, the median full-cycle tracking deviation was 4.9% of a 0.70 saturation target, equal to that of a tuned proportional-integral (PI) controller, while the PGML controller reached the target without overshoot in the median and applied approximately 4% less irrigation. Moderate physics guidance reduced long-horizon prediction error by approximately 30% relative to data-only training and reduced irrigation-bound activity, but slightly worsened closed-loop tracking. For a matched prediction workload, the surrogate was approximately 70 times faster than the numerical solver, and batched evaluation cost under 2 ms per column for 5000 columns. The results support a reusable physics-guided surrogate for large-scale saturation control in simulation.

title: An Adjoint Krylov Approach to Parameter Inference for Affine Families of Linear Evolution Equations
abstract: This paper introduces an adjoint Krylov method for parameter inference in large, sparse linear evolution equations whose system matrices depend affinely on unknown coefficients. We estimate these coefficients from discrete observations by constructing one forward and one adjoint Krylov approximation on each observation interval. Quadrature of the resulting bilinear form gives the full coefficient gradient through sparse matrix-vector products, without evaluating a separate Frechet derivative in every operator direction. We separate the gradient error into forward, adjoint, and quadrature terms and derive residual-based bounds for Markov and Lindblad generators. We also identify cases in which heuristic stopping estimates become small before the gradient has converged. With workspace reuse, we compute library gradients for a 12-qubit Lindblad generator with dimension 1.7 x 10^7 on a single machine with 16 GB of memory. Experiments on chemical master, Kuramoto-Sivashinsky, and Lindblad equations demonstrate accurate gradients and parameter recovery.

title: Linker stretching optimizes bonding entropy in sticker-spacer condensates
abstract: Phase separating biopolymers are often described by the sticker-spacer model, which accounts for non-attractive linkers that connect discrete attractive moieties. "Associative polymer" theories describe these systems as two coexisting fluids of stickers and spacers, respectively. In such theories the stickers and spacers are decoupled in the sense that sticker binding does not affect spacer conformations or vice versa. Informed by coarse-grained simulations, we develop a phenomenological mean-field theory to determine the microscopic coupling between the sticker and spacer degrees of freedom. Accounting for linkers connecting adjacent spacers introduces free energy contributions due to conformational entropy of the spacer and the binding combinatorics of the stickers. These contributions have opposite dependencies on spacer length because longer spacers allow a greater volume to search for binding partners but incur a greater entropy cost upon bond formation. The length dependent terms from these contributions cancel leaving a length-independent elastic term arising from the fact that a small amount of spacer stretching lowers the free energy by increasing the number of possible binding partners. The cancellation of spacer length from the theory justifies the decoupling approximation and supports mean-field treatments of heterogeneous spacers.

title: Orbital Coupling Engineering through P-Block Metal Doping in NiFe Layered Double Hydroxides for Enhanced Anion-Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
abstract: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a major kinetic bottleneck in anodic water splitting because of sluggish adsorption and desorption kinetics of O-containing intermediates. Optimizing the adsorption strength of various O-containing intermediates in accordance with the Sabatier principle involves the precise tuning of the active-site electronic structure. Herein, we explore a p-block metal-assisted synergism regulation strategy in NiFe layered double hydroxides (LDHs) by introducing group-13 elements (Al, Ga, In) as dopants.

title: Data fusion of high-performance liquid chromatography and near-infrared spectroscopy with explainable machine learning for commercial origin authentication of Cimicifugae Rhizoma
abstract: Multi-instrument data fusion combined with explainable machine learning offers a powerful strategy for complex sample authentication, yet quantitative attribution of each analytical source's contribution remains an unresolved methodological challenge. This study presents a two-platform data fusion framework integrating high-performance liquid chromatography with ultraviolet detection (providing both untargeted chromatographic fingerprints and targeted phenolic acid markers) and near-infrared spectroscopy, and employs SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) TreeExplainer for quantitative…

title: Real-World Adaptation and External Validation of Machine-Learning Impedance Spectroscopy for Immediate Postpartum Detection of Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injuries
abstract: Obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) requires immediate postpartum recognition for primary repair. Diagnosis relies primarily on clinical examination, as endoanal ultrasound (EAUS) is rarely a bedside option. Therefore, objective diagnostic assessment is most needed during the first postpartum hours. However, it is challenging to obtain the anatomically verified data needed to develop diagnostic technologies for this clinical window. We evaluated the translation of a machine-learning-assisted impedance spectroscopy model into its intended immediate postpartum setting.

title: An integrated prediction model using machine learning and dynamics simulation for the selection of transdermal penetration enhancers
abstract: Penetration enhancers (PEs) are widely used in transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) due to their cost-effectiveness and excellent biocompatibility. However, the rapid selection of PEs for TDDS is hindered by two critical challenges: first, in vitro permeation tests (IVPT) are costly and time consumption; second, the datasets for drug-PE matching are relatively limited.
venue: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society

title: Latent-Space Residue-Pair Networks from Molecular Dynamics Distinguish Ligand-Activated and SAVI-Associated STING
abstract: Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) provides an informative model system for developing methods to extract and compare residue-pair fluctuation patterns from molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. We combined a one-dimensional convolutional autoencoder trained on apo STING with temporal mean pooling, Mahalanobis-distance clustering, and residue-pair similarity networks to compare apo, ligand-bound, and SAVI-associated multi-mutant datasets using 25-dimensional latent descriptors. Networks constructed from clusters capturing state-dependent fluctuation patterns showed lid-dominated organization in the ligand-bound dataset and a1b1-enriched, structurally distributed relationships involving residue 281 in the multi-mutant dataset. These findings identify contrasting residue-pair fluctuation signatures in the analyzed trajectories and provide an interpretable framework for generating hypotheses about ligand-associated and mutation-associated dynamic allostery.
